surface-probe.look: Slope of a 5-octave simplex FBm is a bright worm-band mask on the steep flanks with dark hairlines on crests and floors; Laplacian is an isotropic band-pass blob field (the 3-tap jet Laplacian shows a hexagonal null pattern in the FFT, the central one does not); Hillshade is a readable relief render; DoubleAngleAspect is a harsh black/white facet map; ShapeSign is a smooth bimodal convex/concave blob mask; Unsharp is the source with crisper edges. None of these is a look in itself, all are masks a graph cannot make today.
surface-probe.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D tetra jet and 6-tap central; z-continuity max 0.029 for dz 1e-3). 4D is the same code with one more axis, not run.
surface-probe.range: slope [-1,0.93] via 1-exp(-k|g|); Laplacian needs a per-source scale (lk 0.01 on simplex, 0.08 saturates); hillshade [-0.76,1]
surface-probe.artifacts: Jet gradient has an O(h) bias of about 1.3h relative (6% at h 0.05, 13% at 0.1) because the simplex stencil's third moment is not zero; central is 1% at 0.05. Jet Laplacian has a hexagonal transfer function. Any output is one derivative order rougher than the source.
surface-probe.node_shape: SurfaceProbe: Source, Output enum {Slope, Hillshade, Directional, NormalX/Y/Z, DoubleAngleAspect, Laplacian, Unsharp, ShapeSign}, Sample Distance (hybrid, floored), Stencil enum {Jet, Central}, Slope Reference, Light X/Y/Z, Output Min/Max. probe_common.h Probe2/Probe3 + StepFloor is the shared kernel for iso-distance, contour-scarp and crest-lines.
surface-probe.port_notes: Step floor settled: naive FD gradient error vs analytic Perlin gradient is 0.6% at origin, 7-20% at 4e4 features for h<=0.01, 45% at 1e5; a k-ulp floor helps only for k~4 (k=32 ruins 1e5 with 52% truncation). Fix: divide by the step the floats actually took, hx=(x+h)-(x-h): 0.2% at 1e5, 2% at 1e6 with h 0.05; then the floor needs k=2 only. Second differences need h >= ~16 ulp (Laplacian error 30% at 4e4 with h 0.05, 9% at h 0.1). Beyond ~1e6 features the source itself is quantized. Port: per-axis central exact-step as default stencil, jet as the cheap option for Slope/Hillshade; floor = Max(h, Abs(pos)*2^-23*k) per lane with k=2, 16 for Hessian outputs.

critic.notes: Not a look, a utility, and the prototyper is wrong that a graph cannot make these masks. I built Slope from real nodes (DomainOffset x4, Subtract x2, PowInt x2, Add, SignedSquareRoot): it renders the same mask, fnlab check 0 FAIL, 26.62 ns AVX2 2D at 5 octaves. Hillshade reads almost the same from a 2 node emboss (Subtract + DomainOffset). It still earns a node, because slope masks are among the most used terrain tools, a preset of 10 nodes is a poor way to get one, and a node can widen its step per lane: the real graph at 1e5 features with a 2 unit offset shows strong diagonal moire. Keep Slope and Laplacian. Drop ShapeSign (a clamped Laplacian at 5 taps gives the same mask), DoubleAngleAspect (jumps), Unsharp (graph). The hexagon in the Laplacian FFT is the Simplex kernel, not the jet stencil: central on Simplex shows the same six nulls, jet on Perlin shows an axis cross. Exact-step divisor is cheap and worth keeping but it is not the 60x fix claimed: that holds only at frequency 1. For the floor use one law, h = hw * max(1, 4 * (|x| 2^-23 / hw)^(1/4)), measured at 3 frequencies and 2 steps: gradient error <= 8.6% at 1e5, 13.9% at 3e5, 23.4% at 1e6 features, against 14.8%, 73.8%, 101% for the 16 ulp floor. Tested on Perlin only, 2 seeds. Not ported to SIMD. Tiling through the 4D torus is untested for a real 4-axis stencil; the 2-axis slope graph passed the seam test.
critic.improved: Slope at h 0.1 instead of 0.03 on 5 octaves: c0 7.80 vs 7.18, max slope 34 vs 94, broad usable mask instead of a hairline clutter. Replacement floor law measured in critic_far.cpp, not yet in the prototype's own kernel.

measured.real_graph_check: 0 FAIL, 2 WARN (3D and 4D continuity, inherited from Simplex radius 0.6). Stencil on X and Y only, 4 FBm taps.
measured.scalar_vs_perlin: stencil=1 6.88x (1 oct), 30.37x (5 oct); jet 5.71x (1 oct), 24.67x (5 oct). The claimed 5.82 is the jet, the stated params are central.
measured.shape_sign_vs_clamped_laplacian: pearson 0.957 to 0.981, sign agreement 0.989 to 0.999. ShapeSign is 9 taps, the Laplacian 5.
measured.real_3d_slope_continuity_worst_ratio: Simplex 1.23 (4D 0.99), Perlin 3.42, SuperSimplex 4.02. The prototype tests 3D on simplex3g r2 0.5, which is not the real 3D Simplex (r2 0.6).

tournament.notes: A utility, not a look, and a graph can make it: real Slope is 26.62/57.88/65.82 ns AVX2 at 5 octaves on 4 FBm taps, check 0 FAIL. It still earns a node because slope masks are among the most used terrain tools, 10 nodes is a poor way to get one, and a node can widen its step per lane: the real graph shows strong moire at 1e5 features with a 2 unit offset. Keep central Slope and Laplacian, plus Signed Distance and Crest as outputs. Hillshade optional, close to a 2 node emboss. Drop ShapeSign: pearson 0.957-0.981 and sign agreement 0.989-0.999 with a clamped Laplacian, at 9 taps vs 5. Drop DoubleAngleAspect (c0 1.03-1.22) and Unsharp (graph). The jet saves one tap in 2D but has 6.3% bias at h 0.05 against 1.1%. Prefer SuperSimplex or Perlin sources in 3D: real Simplex worst ratio 1.23 vs 4.02. Not ported to SIMD; 4-axis stencil tiling untested.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: gradient-only jet (D+1 Perlin evals) 3.3 / 8.8 / 21.5 ns; central exact-step (2D+1 evals) 5.5 / 15 / 39 ns; multiply by octaves for FBm sources; Hessian (9/19/33 taps) 10 / 42 / 140 ns

artist-terrain.note: No look at all (slope worms, Laplacian blobs). Slope mask is a top terrain tool and the 10-node graph moires at far coords. Ship with Slope, Laplacian, Signed Distance, Crest.

artist-material.note: Dull to look at and I do not care. Slope, normal and curvature masks drive every layered material.

voxel-engineer.note: Dull image, daily tool: slope masks drive materials. Graph is 57.88 ns 3D at 5 octaves measured. Would be far cheaper with a gradient path.

maintainer.note: Slope, Laplacian, hillshade from D+1 or 2D+1 source taps, 3.3 ns est on Perlin. A graph does it in 10 nodes at 27 ns, so this is a utility that earns its place on use frequency, plus the far-coordinate exact-step and fourth-root step findings. Not a look.

master.one_liner: The sampled-derivative building block: value, gradient, Laplacian, Hessian and iso-distance from one node at the cheapest possible stencil.
master.look:
Slope: bright ridges and cliff bands, dark flats - the mask everyone uses for rock-vs-grass; Laplacian: thin bright ridgelines and dark valley lines (a pointwise 'ridge detector'); Hillshade: an instantly readable relief render usable as a texture mask (sun-facing snow, shadowed moss).
[SourceCurvature, graph-meta-filters] Ridge strength on a Simplex FBm gives a smooth, organic vein / crack network that follows the crests of the source (proto sheetC m1): thin bright filaments with Y-junctions, nothing like Cellular F2-F1 (which is polygonal) or Ridged FBm (which is a different field). Valley strength is the dual network. Laplacian is an isotropic band-pass of any source (a Mexican-hat of Cellular gives rims). LensDensity at k ~ 1/f^2 gives an underwater-caustic net (proto sheetA m0; on Simplex base it needs a larger k than Perlin). Uses: crack/vein textures that are coherent with a terrain, river/ridge masks for an existing heightfield, rims around cells, detail placement by convexity (rock on convex, sediment on concave), caustic textures.
master.algorithm:
Stencil choice by Output enum. Jet stencil: simplex v_i at step h, with sum v_i = 0 and sum v_i v_i^T = (D+1)/D I. g = D/((D+1)h) sum f_i v_i. Laplacian = 2D/h^2 (mean f_i - f_0). Outputs needing it: Slope |g|*FeatureRef, Slope Angle (polynomial atan), Directional Derivative g.u, Relief (normalised sun term), Normal component g_x/sqrt(1+|g|^2), Laplacian, Unsharp S - k*lap, Double-angle Aspect (gx^2-gy^2)/|g|^2, IsoDistance S/sqrt(|g|^2+e^2) (uniform width bands). Hessian stencil adds ShapeSign tr(H)/(sqrt(D)||H||_F), Mean Curvature, det(H) for passes. Blur stencils: Vogel disc or rotated-grid taps with box or Gaussian weights, with hybrid radius (spatially varying blur).

[GradientFilter, distribution-topology] h = Epsilon (world units, e.g. 0.05 x feature size). Stencil evals of the source S:
  f0 = S(x); f+a = S(x + h e_a), f-a = S(x - h e_a) for each axis (2d evals); for Hessian modes also f(+-h e_a +-h e_b) for a<b (2d(d-1) evals).
  g_a = (f+a - f-a)/(2h); H_aa = (f+a + f-a - 2 f0)/h^2; H_ab = (f++ - f+- - f-+ + f--)/(4h^2)
Modes:
  Slope: |g|            Directional: dot(g, L) with L = (Light X,Y,Z,W) normalised at param-set
  Laplacian: sum_a H_aa
  Ridge / Valley (2D): m = (H_xx+H_yy)/2, r = sqrt(((H_xx-H_yy)/2)^2 + H_xy^2); lambda_max = m + r, lambda_min = m - r; Ridge = max(0, -lambda_min) * (optional) exp(-|g|^2/s^2) to keep only crest lines; Valley symmetric. 3D: second derivative across the gradient, n = g/|g|, kappa_n = n^T H n, and the transverse Laplacian L_t = trace(H) - kappa_n as a cheap ridge measure (no eigen solve), or 2 power-iteration steps for lambda_max.
  ContourCurvature (2D): kappa = (H_xx g_y^2 - 2 H_xy g_x g_y + H_yy g_x^2) / max(|g|^3, eps) (curvature of the level set through x; sign = concave vs convex side). 3D: mean curvature of the level set = (trace(H) - n^T H n)/|g|.
Out scaled by Output Min/Max; Slope optionally through 1 - exp(-k slope) to bound it.
master.why_new: Every graph that wants slope logic is impossible today: there is no multi-sample node, and Fade and Remap only see values. This is the piece that unlocks slope-weighted detail, slope-driven biome mixing, uniform-width lines. It also defines the shared internal helper used by most other nodes on this list. A dedicated node is justified since finite differences cannot be wired with existing nodes except by hand with DomainOffset, at twice the taps and with no scale compensation.
master.simd_plan: Cost in source evaluations, 2D/3D/4D. Gradient only: 3/4/5 (central differences would be 4/6/8). Jet, value+gradient+Laplacian: 4/5/6. Full Hessian: 6/10/15 with first-order mixed terms, 9/19/33 symmetric. Blur: K taps, independent of D but quality falls. On Perlin, jet = 4.4/11/26 ns; on 5-octave FBm multiply by 5. Hybrids add one evaluation each at p only, not per tap. Nesting multiplies, so a Slope of a Slope is (D+2)^2; for a cheap second derivative use the Hessian stencil instead. Taps compose fine with lanes unrelated in space. GeneratorCache gives no savings since taps differ in position.
master.continuity: One order lower than the source: C1 source gives C0 slope. Slope has a cone-shaped kink at extrema unless regularised, sqrt(|g|^2+e^2) smooths it. On Cellular F1 sources, gradient outputs jump at cell walls but stay finite since h is finite.
master.params: Output enum, Sample Distance h (hybrid; clamp to a positive floor), Direction X/Y/Z/W (hybrid for directional), Slope Reference (world units per feature so that output stays scale invariant), e (regularise), Source.
master.risks:
Float error: differencing at far coordinates loses bits; with h = 0.05 feature at x=1e5 and small feature scale, error is noticeable, so h needs a floor in ulps. Slope range depends on the source, so outputs need a stated reference or measured normalise. ShapeSign on single-octave Perlin clearly revealed the lattice, so it is better on Simplex or SuperSimplex. Forward stencils leak h^2 bias from the Laplacian into the gradient; symmetric stencils are an enum away.
[SourceCurvature, graph-meta-filters] Second differences amplify float error by 1/e^2: with e=0.03 and far coordinates (|pos|>1e4) precision collapses; needs a documented minimum Epsilon or an internal clamp relative to |pos|. 3D eigenvalues via Jacobi add ~60 ops; invariants-only (Laplacian/det/Frobenius) may be enough for most looks. Expensive on fractal sources; recommend GeneratorCache is irrelevant (different positions) so cost is real.
master.cost_note: On Perlin, jet = 4.4/11/26 ns; on 5-octave FBm multiply by 5.
master.variant_notes: Nine proposals of derivative analysis of a source; shared helper for many other nodes on this list. Outputs: DX..DW, slope, normal, hillshade, aspect, Laplacian, ridge/valley via Hessian eigenvalues, Gaussian/mean curvature, NormalRGBA8. The same graph needs about 12 nodes and there is no plain Sqrt node.

queue.name: SurfaceProbe
queue.reason: Slope, Laplacian and curvature of any graph from one jet stencil (J1, J2 top pick). Not a look but a prerequisite for a dozen entries. Verify the step floor at far coordinates.

iso-distance.look: Band: a coastline of visibly constant width around the zero set, even on the 5-octave FBm, where the naive abs(f)<w band in the same frame shows fat blobs at saddles and hairlines on steep flanks. On 5 octaves there are small specks where fine octaves make tiny zero crossings and near critical points; 3 octaves is almost perfectly clean; 7 octaves gets fuzzy at h 0.03. Contours (Period 0.6) is a topographic map with uniform line weight. Stripes with 3 Newton steps is the eikonal fingerprint/zebra labyrinth with a ring FFT and knots along the medial axis; with it=0 the stripes degenerate into compressed interference away from the zero set, so the Period/Stripes output needs the Newton walk. Terrace gives risers of constant plan width (the naive terrace smears risers on gentle ground and crowds them on steep). Canyon cuts an incision of constant width with sheer walls. 3D: a shell of constant thickness around the isosurface (vol).
iso-distance.dims: 2D and 3D measured (3D tetra or 6-tap central; shell volume rendered; z-continuity max 0.11 at oct5, 0.06 at oct3, because the band edge is a steep ramp). 4D is the same pack code, not run.
iso-distance.range: [-1,1] by construction (band, stripes, contours); signed mode clamps d/MaxDist
iso-distance.artifacts: Specks at critical points of the source (gradient floor hides most), more with more octaves; Sample Distance should default relative to the finest source detail (h about 1/10 of the finest wavelength). Newton it=1 on the band adds specks (c0ratio drops to 1.0) so first order is the default; Stripes have knots at the medial axis and break up on 2+ octave sources; band edge is C0 only.
iso-distance.node_shape: IsoDistance: Source, Level (hybrid), Period (0 = single level), Output enum {Signed, Band, Stripes, Terrace, Canyon, Scarp}, Width (hybrid, world units), Riser/Canyon Depth, Sample Distance, Gradient Floor, Iterations (0..3, needed for Stripes), Max Step, Output Min/Max.
iso-distance.port_notes: Shares the Probe stencil; d = wrap(S-L, P) / Max(|g|, GradFloor). Exact-step divisor keeps the band identical at 1e5 features; at 1e6 the source is quantized. Measured scalar: 6.69x perlin (1 octave, central), 6.28x (jet), 28.3x on a 5-octave simplex FBm (re-measured), stripes it=3 18.2x; check c0ratio 4.99 (oct3), 3.34 (oct5 h0.03), 5.5 (oct5 h0.06). Newton loop is a fixed count, branch-free with a Min on the step scale. Canyon and Terrace need the true source height as well as d (already in f0). Scarp output folds in contour-scarp.
iso-distance.params_text: mode=1,oct=5,w=0.06,h=0.06,tapmean=1,gfloor=0.000001,sflo=0.5 (5 octave band; oct=3 for clean lines); mode=2,oct=3,P=0.6,w=0.05,h=0.06,tapmean=1,gfloor=0.000001,sflo=0.5 (contours)

critic.params: mode=1,oct=5,w=0.06,h=0.06,tapmean=1,gfloor=0.000001,sflo=0.5 (5 octave band); same with oct=3 for clean lines; mode=2,oct=3,P=0.6,w=0.05,h=0.06,tapmean=1,gfloor=0.000001,sflo=0.5 (contours)
critic.notes: On a 5 octave source the width is not constant. Measured against an exact distance transform, the 10% to 90% spread at the band edge is 3.28x at h 0.06 where the naive abs band is 4.77x, and at w 0.2 the gain almost vanishes (4.02 vs 4.20). The real benefit at 5 octaves is continuity: 2.6% of the core is lost against 11.8% for the naive band, no hairlines on steep flanks. It is near constant on 1 octave (1.07x) and good on 3 (1.89x, 1.63x with the fix). This is a small real graph, not a new capability: I built the band from real nodes, same look, 44.49 ns AVX2 at 5 octaves against an estimated 32 ns for a node. So it should not be its own node, but it is worth one enum value on surface-probe because the kernel is the same taps. The prototype only works at Feature Scale about 2.5: its Gradient Floor 0.1 is absolute and at Feature Scale 100 turns the band into fat mush. Must be fixed before a port. 3D is the best argument: constant thickness shell is visibly more even than the abs shell, which goes thick and thin (vol_shell). Outputs I would cut after looking at them on seeds 42 and 7 at 3 octaves: Terrace (the plain value terrace looks crisper, the distance risers look smeared), Canyon (blue flats with thin creases, pillars at 5 octaves). Wide view at 5 octaves is a dense wiry web with knots, usable only as fine detail. Exact-step divisor makes no visible difference to the band at these settings. 4D and tiling not tested for a 4-axis stencil.
critic.improved: Two changes that use only the existing stencil taps. (1) Residual = mean of all taps instead of the centre tap. (2) Gradient floor = max(g, 0.5 h (|hxx|+|hyy|)) instead of absolute 0.1. Ground truth p90/p10 of true distance at the band edge, 3 seeds: 5 octaves 3.28 to 2.61, 3 octaves 1.89 to 1.63, missed core 2.6% to 0.2% at 5 octaves. The floor is scale free: at Feature Scale 100 the prototype's floor gives median width 2.94 w and 34% false band, the new floor 0.92 w and 1.1 to 1.7%. Cost: 5% in the scalar proto, no new taps. Price: c0 at 5 octaves 5.45 to 3.27 (seed 1337), 3.46 and 4.02 on seeds 42 and 90210. At 3 octaves c0 6.09, 7.63, 7.61, better than the prototype's 4.99.

measured.step_changes_width: oct5 median true distance 0.082 at h 0.03, 0.068 at h 0.06, 0.062 at h 0.10; missed core 1.8%, 2.6%, 6.0%
measured.real_graph_check: 0 FAIL, 3 WARN (3D 2.16, 4D 2.72, tile seam ratio 3.96). Stencil on X and Y only in this graph.
measured.divisor_at_far: band with naive vs exact divisor, 3 octaves fq 0.4: mean difference 0.84 of 255 at far 1e5 world, 0.95 at far 2.5e5 world, no pixel off by more than 12
measured.scalar_vs_perlin: 6.77x (1 oct), 29.20x (5 oct) before my edits, matching the claim. Later scalar timings include extra std::map parameter lookups per sample and are not comparable.

tournament.notes: Not constant width on 5 octaves (3.28 against naive 4.77, and 4.02 vs 4.20 at w 0.2), near constant on 1 octave (1.07), decent on 3 (1.89). Thin even coastlines at 1-3 octaves look good; the 5 octave wide view is a wiry web with knots. Same look from a real graph at 44.49 ns (estimated 32 ns as a node), so it should be one enum value on the probe, not a node. Band and contours are Abs + Remap on Signed; Period stays in the node because wrap must happen before the divide. The 3D constant-thickness shell is visibly more even than the abs shell, which goes thick and thin, and is its best use. Cut Terrace (value terrace looks crisper by eye on seeds 42 and 7), Canyon, Scarp and Stripes outputs, and the Newton loop. The exact-step divisor makes no visible difference to the band: mean 0.84-0.95 of 255. Must fix the absolute Gradient Floor before any port.

master.one_liner: Divides any smooth source by its gradient length to get an approximate world-unit distance to an iso-level, giving constant-width lines, rivers, bevels and terraces.
master.look:
Even-width contour lines, rivers and roads along the zero set of a low-frequency noise. Plateaus get constant-width cliffs, like bevelled masks or rice-paddy terraces. Rescaling source amplitude does not change the output. Look-tested (lm_lens modes 1 and 3): naive |f| shows blobs at saddles and hairlines on slopes, while IsoDistance stays nearly uniform with faint smudges at f~0, grad~0. The Newton version is sharper but adds specks, so first order is the recommended default.
[LevelSetDistance, terrain-landforms] One continuous meandering incision of uniform width through any terrain, with flat floor, vertical or terraced walls, no pinch-outs where the source is steep and no bloat where it is flat. Prototyped: Canyon (terraced walls) and Slot (narrow). Also coastline cliffs (Level = sea level of a continent noise), mesa rims (Level = caprock elevation), rivers for texture masks.
master.algorithm:
h = Epsilon. f0 = S(x) - Level(x) (Level hybrid). g = central differences (2d evals), n = max(|g|, GradFloor).
If Period P > 0: r = f0 - P * round(f0 / P)   // signed offset to the nearest contour of the family Level + kP, in [-P/2, P/2]
else r = f0.
d = r / n.
Newton refinement (Iterations = 0..2, same count for all lanes): x1 = x - d * g / |g|; f1 = wrap(S(x1) - Level); d = d + f1 / n (optionally recompute g at x1 for a second-order correction).
Out = clamp(d, -MaxDist, MaxDist) (world units; VariableRange maps to +-1 with MaxDist). Band use: Abs(out) < w is a band of true width 2w around the iso-level.

[IsoDistance, libs-modifiers] f0 = Source(p) - Level; for each axis g_i = (Source(p + h*e_i) - Level - f0) / h; L2 = sum(g_i^2); d = f0 / sqrt(L2 + eps). Modes: Signed: out = clamp(d / MaxDist, -1, 1). Band: out = clamp(|d| / Width, 0, 1) * 2 - 1. IsoLines(N): t = f0*N; e = (t - round(t)) / N; d = e / sqrt(L2 + eps), then Band. ContourTerrace(N, Riser): t = f0*N; r = floor(t); fr = t - r - 0.5; a = sign(fr) * max(|fr| / (N * sqrt(L2 + eps) * Riser), 2*|fr|); a = clamp(a, -1, 1); out = (r + hermite(a*0.5 + 0.5)) / N. The 2*|fr| term forces the riser to saturate at band edges, which keeps it C0 where contours crowd. Optional Newton refinement: st = f0 / (L2 + eps), limited to MaxStep; p1 = p - st*g; d = sign(f0)*|st|*|g| + f(p1) / |grad f(p1)| (doubles the cost).
master.why_new: abs(noise) < w has width proportional to 1/|grad f|, so a river cannot be asked for in world units today. Width becomes a real length, independent of source amplitude and octave count. It also gives Terrace a riser width that does not collapse on steep ground. No existing node exposes a gradient, and the graph version needs dim+1 source copies plus a dozen operators.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free, generic GenT over the position pack, no lattice. Source evaluated dim+1 times: 3/4/5 evals in 2D/3D/4D, so 3.3/8.8/21.5 ns on Perlin (3x/4x/5x Perlin). InvSqrt or Sqrt once. Fractal sources multiply accordingly. 4D output inherits GenTileable2D periodicity because it is a pure function of the 4D coordinates.
master.continuity: C0 wherever the source is C1, since the sqrt(L2+eps) denominator is smooth and positive. Measured c0ratio 6.8 (band) and 7.9 (terrace). C1 is lost at the band clamp and along |d|.
master.params: Source; Level (hybrid); Period (float, 0 = single level); Epsilon; Gradient Floor; Iterations (int 0..2); Max Dist; Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Estimate is only valid near the level set, so keep MaxDist under the source feature size. Smudges at critical points. Needs C1 sources (not CellularValue or White). h must suit the source scale and survive far coordinates. Sources with kinks (Abs, F1) give a usable but biased estimate.
[IsoDistance, distribution-topology] Far from the level set the value is only a distance estimate (clamp it); near saddles/plateaus of the source the estimate overshoots. Epsilon must be below the finest source detail. Cost multiplies the source cost by 5-7.
sources: Inigo Quilez distance estimation of implicit functions (from memory, not consulted)
Taubin 1994, Distance approximations for rasterizing implicit curves (the |f|/|grad f| estimate)
from memory, not consulted: Taubin 1994 'Distance approximations for rasterizing implicit curves'

master.variant_notes: f/|grad f| with band, canyon, shell, contour-period and terrace outputs. Tests: first order is the recommended default, as Newton is sharper but adds specks. Tetrahedral stencil from TaubinDistance is the cheapest gradient.

queue.name: IsoDistance

crest-lines.look: On 1-2 octave simplex: thin, even-width crest (white) and valley (black) lines with free ends, Y-branches and gentle meanders, like a drainage or leaf-vein map; no closed loops, nothing like Ridged or F2-F1. The plain ridge-strength (-lambda_min) comparison is a blobby variable-width mask, so the Newton distance is what makes the lines. Stable, not noisy, at 1-2 octaves (c0ratio 7.9 / 6.7). At 3 octaves the lines fragment into short dashes and the sheet gets busy (c0ratio 2.1); raising the step alone (h 0.08) barely helps (c0ratio 2.4, still dashed), while h 0.05 with regularise c=2 and width 0.08 reconnects most lines into a continuous branching net with a few dashes left (c0ratio 3.6), so 3 octaves is usable but never as clean as 1-2. Perlin base at fq 0.6 showed no obvious right-angle segments. Relief renders as a hedge-maze of constant-width walls on the crests. 3D (19-tap Hessian, power iteration) gives fragmented plates, not useful as a volume.
crest-lines.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 3D is sheets/plates (vol rendered), z-continuity max 0.97 for dz 1e-3 shows per-lane eigenvector flips in 3D. 4D not attempted.
crest-lines.artifacts: Dashes and gaps where the strength mask -l-|m| crosses its threshold; small speckle patches at saddles; at far coordinates the second differences break first: at 1e5 features with h 0.03 (2.5 ulp) the lines sit in a hash of noise, a 16-ulp floor (h 0.19) restores clean but thicker lines, so the Hessian stencil is limited to roughly 1e4 features at the default h or must widen with |x|.
crest-lines.node_shape: CrestLines: Source, Mode {Crest, Valley, Both}, Line Width (hybrid), Strength Min/Max, Regularise c, Sample Distance. Could also be an Output of SurfaceProbe's Hessian stencil if the eigen solve is accepted there.
crest-lines.port_notes: 2D eigenpairs closed form (two candidate eigenvectors, pick the longer; the other is the perpendicular). 3D needs power iteration (4 steps here) and the 'other eigenvalue' is only a trace proxy; eigenvector flips make 3D jumpy. Hessian wants h >= 16 ulp(|pos|). Costly on FBm sources and fragments above 2-3 octaves: feed it the low octaves only.

critic.notes: Stable against the step at 1 to 2 octaves (IoU 0.995, 0.982), noisy above that (0.956 at 3, 0.659 at 5). Stable is not connected: only 13 to 24% of line area at 1 to 2 octaves sits in pieces longer than 3 units, the wide view at 2 octaves is a lacy net with many dots and stubs. Honest look: a drainage or vein map in 2D. 'Nothing like F2-F1' is too strong: a thin warped masked F2-F1 reads as a similar crack network at 8.38 ns, though its lines are straighter with 120 degree joints and its FFT has a cross. What no graph gives is lines on the ridges of your own source, which is the actual use: feed the low octaves of a terrain, get ridge and drainage masks that line up with it. The 3D fix is the surprise: membranes with windows, neither the Abs pretzel nor the flat F2-F1 polyhedra. Crest relief is a hedge maze, not terrain. Limits: 9 taps 2D, 19 taps 3D, about 12.8x Simplex before the eigen solve; no closed form in 4D, so it will not tile; acos needs a polynomial. Real source not tested through the 19-tap path.
critic.improved: (1) Scale free: prototype defaults are absolute and render BLANK at Feature Scale 100 (min -1, max -1, std 0). Regulariser rc |g| / h and strength / (|l|+|m|+eps): same lines at Feature Scale 2.5 and 100. c0 6.80, 6.88, 5.19 over 3 seeds. Sparser than the absolute thresholds unless a and b are lowered, I did not tune that further. (2) Closed-form 3D eigenpairs with the true middle eigenvalue instead of 4 power iterations: z-continuity max 0.50 to 0.031 (1 octave), 1.02 to 0.080 (2 octaves, seed 42); fragments become a connected membrane. (3) Warp outside the probe keeps the Hessian on 1 octave and gives irregular crack lines, c0 7.8 and 6.8 on two seeds, 3.6 on a third. (4) Far: root-4 step law, cleaner than 2 ulp at 1e5 features and about equal to 16 ulp there, much better further out by the numbers.

master.one_liner: Uniform-width ridge and valley lines of any field by a Newton projection on the Hessian. Open branching drainage networks with no simulation.
master.look: Thin, even-width branching, meandering lines with free ends, like river maps, leaf veins or mountain spines. Interleaved crest and valley networks in one output look like a drainage map. Very different from FractalRidged and F2-F1, whose lines are closed loops. Uses: rivers, roads along valleys, ridge masks, cracks, veins.
master.algorithm: Hessian H by minimal stencil: 2D 6 taps (9 for symmetric), 3D 10, 4D 15. Crest: take the most negative eigenvalue l with eigenvector e, other eigenvalue m. Across-crest Newton distance d = |g.e| / (|l| + c). Line = (1 - smoothstep(0,w,d)) * smoothstep(a,b, -l - |m|). Valley uses the largest eigenvalue with the sign flipped. Eigenvector 2D closed form: e proportional to (H_xy, l-H_xx) or (l-H_yy, H_xy), selected by the larger norm. 3D/4D: 2-3 steps of power iteration on (sI - H), starting from g. The mask -l-|m| reaches 0 at umbilics, which hides the eigenvector ambiguity there.
master.why_new: Gives the true topographic ridge and valley skeleton, with dangling ends and tree-like branching, which level-set based lines cannot have. Pointwise river-like lines that actually lie in the valleys of the terrain they were computed from are hard to get today. Width is in world units and independent of steepness.
master.simd_plan: Taps 6-9 / 10 / 15. On Perlin about 7-10 / 22 / 65 ns (scalar 9-tap version 8.3x perlin2). Eigen solve is closed form in 2D; fixed power iteration in 3D and 4D, with Sqrt and masks only. Fractal sources multiply cost; compute the Hessian on the lower octaves only by giving the node a low-octave source.
master.continuity: C0 by construction with the umbilic mask. Measured c0ratio rises with width (1.4 at w=0.08, 6.2 at w=0.3 on one octave), consistent with thin steep lines, not jumps. Should be verified with fnlab. Line ends fade via the strength mask.
master.params: Line Width w (hybrid), Strength thresholds a,b, Mode enum (Crest, Valley, Both signed), Sample Distance h (hybrid). h should be about 1/20 of the source's finest feature.
master.risks: Second differences amplify lattice artifacts and float error: Perlin axis bias appears as occasional right-angle segments, and far coordinates need larger h. Not a real hierarchical river network: no guaranteed connectivity or flow-order widening. In 3D the lines become sheets, and whether that is useful is unproven.
master.cost_note: On Perlin about 7-10 / 22 / 65 ns (scalar 9-tap version 8.3x perlin2).

contour-scarp.look: Relief: flat-topped mesas and table mountains with near-vertical walls of constant width and a concave talus apron of constant width, the lowlands returning to the source below the toe. Reads as proper mesa country. Stacked bands give cuesta-like stepped hills with every riser the same width. Edge noise crenulates the rim in plan; the first attempt made the plateau tops messy, a smaller cap amplitude fixed it. The naive version (profile on value, what Terrace/Remap can do) is not dramatically worse in this scene: its cliff bands broaden on gentle slopes and thin on steep ones, visible but subtle at this source. The 2D gray sheet is a plateau mask with a dark cliff band.
contour-scarp.dims: 2D measured; 3D runs (same profile on the 3D distance, z-continuity max 0.01) but a mesa profile has no clear 3D meaning beyond a shell thickness.
contour-scarp.range: [-0.6,0.33] with the defaults (height units of the source); needs Output Min/Max
contour-scarp.artifacts: Cliff width widens or vanishes at saddles and summits of the source where the gradient floor takes over; vertical slivers where the source wiggles across the level; pw>2 gives a visible hard edge at the cap (C0).
contour-scarp.node_shape: Either an Output of IsoDistance {Scarp} with Cliff Width/Height, Talus Width/Height, Cap Detail (hybrid), Edge Noise (hybrid into Level), Band Spacing; or a ScarpProfile modifier on IsoDistance's Signed output.
contour-scarp.port_notes: Literally Profile(d) with d from the iso-distance kernel plus a smooth max against the source: same taps, same floor, same Level/Period handling. The profile needs 5 scalars (cliff width/height, exponent, talus width/height), a lot for one Output mode, so the cleaner split is an IsoDistance Signed output feeding a small ScarpProfile value modifier (which would also work on CellularDistance F1 for crater rims). Stacked bands need cliff+talus height to equal the Spacing to stay C0 at band edges.

master.one_liner: Uses the first-order distance to a source's level set to apply a cliff, talus and plateau profile in world units, regardless of source slope. The f/|grad f| approximation is known from SDF rendering; the terrain node is the variation.
master.look: Mesas, buttes, table mountains and escarpments with constant-width vertical walls and aprons of scree. Plateau tops are flat, and the rim is fractal in plan view. Also useful for beaches and shore shelves of constant width.
master.algorithm: h=S(p); grad by forward differences (dim extra evals). L=Level+EdgeNoise(p). d=(h-L)/max(|grad|,eps), clamped to the profile range. Mesa profile: for d>=0, Z=Cap (+CapDetail*small amp). For -Wc<=d<0, Z=Cap-Hc*(-d/Wc)^p (cliff). For the next Wt, a concave talus curve drops by Ht. out=SmoothMax(Base(h), Z), so below the talus the source's own lowlands return. Multi-band option: repeat Levels at fixed spacing, with band index by floor((h-L0)/spacing), to get stacked cliff bands of constant width. Use with fractal EdgeNoise to get crenulated rims and side embayments while the cross-section stays physically constant.
master.why_new: Terrace and Remap operate on height, so cliff width varies inversely with source slope: smeared on gentle slopes and hairline on steep ones. Graphs have no gradient access, so world-space profiles are not possible today. This separates plan-form fractal detail from cross-section, which answers how detail stays plausible.
master.simd_plan: Branch free: 1+dim source evals plus EdgeNoise, then Select and Min/Max. 2D 3x, 3D 4x, 4D 5x source cost. GenT works for every dimension and keeps tiling. Cheap relative to what it provides.
master.continuity: C0 with the eps floor and clamp if the source is continuous; forward differences at a finite step stay continuous even on C0 sources.
master.params: Source, Level (hybrid), Edge Noise (hybrid), Cliff Width and Height, Talus Width and Height, Cap Detail (hybrid), Band Spacing (float, 0 = single), Gradient Step (float), Eps (float).
master.risks: Not tested. First-order distance is wrong near saddles and maxima, where the gradient vanishes, so cliffs may widen or vanish there. Gradient Step must exceed the finest source wavelength or the distance becomes noisy, so feed low octaves and add detail afterward.

queue.reason: World-unit cliffs and talus regardless of source slope, the control Terrace lacks. Untested and saddles break the distance. May end up an output of iso-distance.

eikonal-stripes.look: Tested as the Stripes output of iso-distance: with 3 Newton steps it is the fingerprint/zebra labyrinth with equal-spaced bands following every coastline, a ring FFT and knots along the medial axis. With it=0 (pure first-order distance) the stripes collapse into compressed interference away from the zero set, so this output needs the Newton walk that the Band output must not use. Breaks up on 2+ octave sources.
eikonal-stripes.dims: 2D rendered; 3D uses the same IsoD3 walk (shells), not separately imaged.
eikonal-stripes.artifacts: Knots and specks at the medial axis and near critical points; c0ratio about 1 by construction (Newton basins).
eikonal-stripes.node_shape: Output {Stripes} of IsoDistance with Wavelength, Iterations (3) and Max Step.

critic.notes: Striking and holds up on a wider window and another seed: long even zebra bands following the source's level sets, tight ring in the FFT, and in 3D agate-like slabs. It is the only thing here that really is constant spacing away from the zero set. But it has jumps by construction: chevrons and knots along the medial axis, noise clusters in the 3D seams. PingPong is 1.29 ns but width varies, thick and thin. lattice-phasor already ships a clean labyrinth (c0 6.8) at about 4 ns, with shorter strokes that do not follow a source. Near a coastline the first-order distance with a triangle wave does the common job, so this does not justify putting a Newton loop into a node. Keep as an example, not a regular output. Breaks up on 2 or more octaves per the prototyper; I did not re-render that beyond s_stripes_oct2.
critic.improved: Tried a fade to grey where the Newton walk has not converged (confw=0.08). It only greys a few patches and does not remove the knots or medial cracks, c0 1.2 against 1.0. Not an improvement, left off. The image records it.

tournament.notes: Striking and holds on a wider window and other seeds: long even zebra bands following the source's level sets, a tight ring FFT, agate-like slabs in 3D. It is the only entry with truly constant spacing away from the zero set. But it jumps by construction (c0 1.00, also 1.01 at it 0), with chevrons and knots on the medial axis and noise clusters in the 3D seams. Costs 20 taps at it 3, 20.45x Perlin in scalar, including parameter lookups from my edits. PingPong is 1.29 ns but width varies. lattice-phasor already ships a clean labyrinth (c0 6.8), about 4.3 ns per its critic, with shorter strokes that do not follow a source. Near a coastline, first-order distance with a triangle wave does the common job. Does not justify a Newton loop in the node; keep as an example.

master.one_liner: Project each sample onto a source's zero set with a fixed number of Newton steps, then turn the travelled distance into constant-wavelength stripes: a Turing or fingerprint labyrinth from plain Perlin.
master.look:
Parallel, equal-spacing bands that follow every coastline of the source, forming a coral / brain / fingerprint / topographic-ripple labyrinth. The FFT shows a clean isotropic ring, which no existing node does, and the histogram is nearly flat. Thresholding gives an even-width labyrinth, usable for reaction-diffusion looks, fingerprints, zebra, dune ripples, wave lines around islands and shells in 3D.
[IsoPhase, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Coral or brain-coral labyrinth, fingerprint whorls, zebra stripes of near-uniform width, parallel bands wrapping every contour with Y-defects along the medial axis. FFT shows a real ring, so it is narrow-band like reaction-diffusion. Raw mode gives a rounded distance-to-coast terrain with creases on the medial axis. Good for zebra or coral masks, topographic contour art, shoreline bands, sdf-based terracing, geology stripes.
master.algorithm: q = p; n0 = S(p). Repeat It times (3): g = grad S(q) by FD; step = S(q)*g / (|g|^2 + Eps^2); clamp |step| to MaxStep (0.5); q -= step. d = |q - p| * sign(n0). Output tri(d / Wavelength)*2 - 1, or d clamped when used as an approximate signed distance. Eps = 0.3 damps the chaos near source critical points. Iso offset: use S - Iso.
master.why_new: PingPong and Terrace make band width depend on slope, so they squeeze and blow out. Here spacing is fixed in world units whatever the source slope. A pointwise fixed-iteration projection gets the reaction-diffusion look without simulation and works over any source graph.
master.simd_plan: Fixed It, no per-lane branching (clamp via Min on a scale factor). Forward differences: (It+1)*(1+D) source evals, so 2D 12, 3D 16, 4D 20. Tetrahedral differences reduce 3D to 12. With a dedicated analytic Perlin gradient it measured 6.3x perlin2 scalar (It=3). Sampling must use per-lane displaced positions, which Gen permits. Dimension-agnostic code via a GenT pack.
master.continuity:
Discontinuous at sparse points. Measured c0ratio about 1, because Newton basins do not exactly follow the medial axis. Most of the area is smooth and bands are C0 at tri peaks.
[IsoPhase, dynamics-iteration] Mathematically C0 (continuous composition, sign flips only where d=0). Numerically very steep at medial axes and near-critical points: measured c0ratio 1.0, max slope about 2000 per unit at Frequency 15.
master.params: Wavelength (hybrid), Iterations (int), Eps (float), Max Step (float), Iso (hybrid), Source, Output (Stripes or Distance).
master.risks:
Small speckled knots remain near source critical points. They are much reduced at Eps 0.3 / It 3, but visible at Eps 0.01 and worsen with more octaves in the source (oct=2 was clearly noisier), so it suits smooth 1-octave sources best. Hillshade through it is harsh. Only the 2D form was run; 3D shells are the same formula, untested.
[IsoPhase, dynamics-iteration] Works best on 1-octave sources; 2+ octaves break into noisy dislocations. Distance is capped at N*MaxStep, so low-gradient regions need the cap to cover half a feature. Small speckle at saddles.
master.cost_note: With a dedicated analytic Perlin gradient it measured 6.3x perlin2 scalar (It=3).
master.variant_notes: Newton projection to the zero set, then sine of the distance: clean FFT ring, equal spacing, single-octave sources work best.
